I will apply one bag of urea and half a bag of DAP that I bought with the little cash left from selling cashew nuts last season, which gives me about 20 kilograms of nitrogen for each hectare. I will also spread compost and manure from my goats because the soil here in Mtwara is sandy and needs something to hold the rains. I will plant the local maize seed I saved from last year since I know it grows here and I cannot risk borrowed money on hybrid seed that might fail if the short rains stop early. My children and I will work this plot for about 105 days over the season, and I will hire two women from the village for 10 days when the weeds come up fast after planting.
